To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

plasma membrane of pea seedling roots and shoots is heterogenous in osmotic water transport and this heterogeneity is associated with the presence of domains with different content of PIP aquaporins and membrane sterols.

the osmotic water flow across the plasma membrane of root and shoot cells of etiolated pea plants is mediated by aquaporins of the PIP1 subfamily, and that the plasma membrane of these cells is heterogeneously distributed in terms of the osmotic water transport activity.

the plasma membrane of pea seedlings root and shoot cells is heterogeneous in osmophility, and this heterogeneity is related with the presence in the membrane of microdomains with a different content of PIP aquaporins and cholesterol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the heterogeneity of pea root and shoot plasma membranes in terms of their osmotic water permeation.
the study of plasma membrane heterogeneity and its role in the water transport in plant cell.
the study of the role of PIP1 and sterols in regulation of osmotic water transport through plasma membranes of pea seedlings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heterogeneity of the osmotic water flow across pea seedlings plasma membranes is related with the presence in the membrane microdomains with different sterol and aquaporin content.
the heterogeneity of the plasma membrane in the osmotic water transport capacity is due to the heterogeneity of sterol distribution and the PIP1 aquaporyns in the membrane.
PIP1 aquporins are not responsible for the water permeability of pea seedling PM, but sterol content in the PM may be responsible for the water transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the plasma membrane from pea seedlings is heterogeneous in osmophility, which can be associated with the presence of domains in the membrane with different content of sterols, and PIP1 and PIP2 aquaporins.
PIP1 aquaglycoproteins are the key factors in regulation of the osmotic water flow across plasma membrane of pea seedlings.
PIP1 aquaglyceroporins are involved in regulation of osmotic water fluxes through plasma membrane of etiolated pea root and shoot cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heterogeneity of plasma membrane in osmotic water transport properties is a common feature for root and shoot cells of etiolated pea.
plasma membrane of pea roots and shoots is a heterogeneous system in terms of osmotic water transport.
the PIP1 aquaglyceroporins and sterols are important for plasma membrane water transport.
